html:
SMTO-GML-0023 — SMTO doesn't recognize that Gmail account name

GUID: 079f3a2c-003e-4179-9fd8-7ef7f160cbda
Slug: gmail-parameter-reference-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was told which Gmail account to use, but the account name it was given isn't written in a form SMTO accepts, for example it contains spaces or an email address. Nothing was done in your mailbox.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In your message, type @ and choose your Gmail account from the list that appears. Choosing from the list inserts the exact account name SMTO uses, without spaces or typos.
  2. If it isn't in the list, open the Parameter Store page, select your Gmail account entry, and select Copy reference to get its exact name. The Parameter Store page holds the saved Gmail accounts and their exact names.
  3. Use that name instead of your email address or a nickname when you ask SMTO again. An email address has an @ in the middle, which SMTO account names can't contain.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the Gmail request using the account you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste passwords or sign-in codes into the conversation while trying account names.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail parameter_key() rejected an account or OAuth app reference that does not match the Parameter Store key pattern (letter, digit or underscore first, then letters, digits, _ . : -) or is longer than 160 characters.

What this means

  • Parameter reference normalization rejects a key outside the supported ASCII grammar or longer than 160 characters. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter reference normalization rejects a key outside the supported ASCII grammar or longer than 160 characters.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact canonical key, including optional leading @ syntax, without placing credentials in it.

How to fix it

  • parameter_key() strips a leading @ and requires KEY_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*$ with length <= 160. Pass the exact Parameter Store key of the Gmail Account or Gmail OAuth App parameter (for example @work_gmail), not an email address or display name; the key is shown on the Parameter Store page and via Copy reference.
  • Select the exact current account/profile Parameter Store reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid exact intended account/app key resolves through Parameter Store.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
